Quotation

/kwoh-TAY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Quotation means a group of words taken from a text or speech and repeated exactly by someone else

Above the gym door, the coach had painted a quotation from a famous marathon runner: "The wall is where the race begins."

Worked Example

For her article on the factory closing, the reporter included a quotation from the plant manager — his exact words, 'We held on as long as we could' — because no rewording of the line carried the same weight.

The manager's words are repeated exactly as he spoke them, taken straight from her interview. That exact, repeated wording from a source is what makes it a quotation.

How Quotation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

excerpt

excerpt: a passage lifted from a longer work, exact words included

citation

citation: quoted words plus the formal pointer to where they came from

quote

quote: the everyday, informal version of the same word

Antonyms

paraphrase

paraphrase: the source's idea restated in different words rather than the exact ones

retelling

retelling: the gist of what was said, reshaped in one's own way

How Strong Is It? — mention → quotation → transcript

mention vs. quotation

mention vs. quotation: A mention simply refers to a source without borrowing any of its words.

transcript vs. quotation

transcript vs. quotation: A transcript reproduces every word of an entire speech, not just one chosen passage.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — quot-

Root — quot-: how many (Latin quot)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act or result of (Latin -atio)

Put it together

Put it together: "Quotation" grew from Latin quot, "how many": medieval scholars 'quoted' a text by numbering its chapters and lines so a passage could be found again. Pointing to the exact spot in a text soon became repeating the exact words from that spot.

Use the root in a new word: quotient

Use the root in a new word: quotient: In math class, Amir learned that the quotient is the answer you get when one number is divided by another.

Word Choice

neutral, academic

Quotation is the word for exact borrowed words, usually set inside quotation marks and credited to their source; the shortened 'quote' is the informal version. If the words are changed at all, it is no longer a quotation but a paraphrase. (In business, a quotation can also mean a stated price — a separate sense the SAT rarely tests.)
